briefs.explicit:
MISSION BRIEF S-009
Units: metres, seconds, kilograms. Time starts at t = 0 when every robot leaves its start location.

Locations (x, y, zone):
- base: (0, 0), outdoor
- office roof: (140, 38), roof
- electrical room: (113, -103), indoor
- workcell West: (-135, 75), indoor
- fuel depot: (43, 123), outdoor
- water tank: (85, 75), outdoor

Robots:
- M1 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 9 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 3060 s, including the return to its start.
- A1 (fixed_arm): installed at workcell West and cannot move; it can only work on tasks located at workcell West. Equipment: robotic arm. Mains-powered (no endurance limit).
- D1 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 6 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg). Endurance: 1260 s, including the return to its start.

Tasks:
- T1: Tighten the valve at workcell West. Location: workcell West. Duration: 240 s. Needs: robotic arm.
- T2: Photograph fuel depot for the condition report. Location: fuel depot. Duration: 60 s. Needs: camera.
- T3: Photograph workcell West for the condition report. Location: workcell West. Duration: 60 s. Needs: camera.
- T4: Inspect office roof with a camera. Location: office roof. Duration: 120 s. Needs: camera. Deadline: finished by t = 360 s.
- T5: Tighten the valve at electrical room. Location: electrical room. Duration: 240 s. Needs: robotic arm. Deadline: finished by t = 1020 s.

Rules:
1. Every task is done by exactly one robot. A robot does its tasks one at a time, in the order you list them, travelling between task locations.
2. A robot can only do a task if it has the needed equipment, enough payload capacity, and can reach the task location.
3. A task that must start after another task waits until that task is finished, even if a different robot does it.
4. Each robot must be back at its start location before its endurance runs out.
5. Every task must be finished by t = 1500 s.

Objective: minimise the finish time of the last task (the makespan).
briefs.informal:
Here's what we need from the robots today.

Positions are in metres from the base at (0, 0). Drones fly straight and can't go indoors; ground robots follow the road grid (so they travel |dx| + |dy|) and can't get onto roofs. Everyone leaves their start spot at time zero.

Places: office roof (140, 38, a rooftop); electrical room (113, -103, indoors); workcell West (-135, 75, indoors); fuel depot (43, 123, outside); water tank (85, 75, outside).

The fleet: M1 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 9 kg, moves at 1 m/s and lasts 51 minutes including getting back. A1 is a robot arm bolted down in workcell West; it can't move but can work on jobs inside workcell West, and it runs on mains power. D1 is a quadcopter at base with a camera; it flies at 6 m/s, can lift 2 kg, and its battery lasts 21 minutes including the flight home.

Jobs:
(T1) Someone has to tighten the valve at workcell West - that takes 4 minutes on site.
(T2) Grab photos of fuel depot for the condition report - that takes 1 minute on site.
(T3) We need pictures of workcell West for the report - that takes 1 minute on site.
(T4) Have a look at office roof - that takes 2 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 6 minutes.
(T5) Someone has to tighten the valve at electrical room - that takes 4 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 17 minutes.

Everything has to be wrapped up within 25 minutes of the start, and the sooner the last job finishes, the better. Every robot has to make it back to where it started before its battery runs out.
